advice_items.canonical_tag: Work Under a Winner First Before Starting
advice_items.quote: I worked in the business so I knew exactly what I needed to do.
advice_items.summary_en: Work inside your target industry first to learn operations hands-on before starting your own company.
advice_items.summary_zh: 创业前先在目标行业打工摸清门道，再动手单干

advice_items.quote: I use rejection as fuel. Every time somebody told me, 'Hey, this will never work,' I was like, you know what? I'll prove it to you... believe in yourself.
advice_items.summary_en: Use rejection and doubters as fuel, believe in yourself, and prove your business concept works.
advice_items.summary_zh: 把拒绝和质疑当成燃料，坚信自己并证明给别人看

advice_items.quote: Once I raised a lot of my own personal equity, about $50,000, I was able to go in and get a small SBA loan for $50,000 and get this dilapidated old restaurant space and do the work myself.
advice_items.summary_en: Earn your initial startup capital through hard work, leverage SBA loans and advisory programs like SBDC and SCORE, and renovate leanly yourself.
advice_items.summary_zh: 苦干攒首笔本金，借SBA贷款低成本自装修起家

advice_items.quote: You have to know your numbers inside and out. You have to believe in them. Low, mediums, and highs.
advice_items.summary_en: Know your financial numbers inside and out, including low (break-even), medium, and high projections.
advice_items.summary_zh: 吃透盈亏平衡与高中低财务预测，熟知所有数字

advice_items.quote: Best negotiation advice I can give anybody is believe in what you're doing and know your numbers inside and out. And don't let people talk you down on your numbers.
advice_items.summary_en: In negotiations, believe in your numbers, refuse to be talked down if the math works, and take the deal elsewhere if needed.
advice_items.summary_zh: 谈判时笃定自身数据不被压价，不合适就换下一家

advice_items.canonical_tag: Use Debt Wisely (Good Debt vs Bad Debt)
advice_items.quote: I almost broke our business. I overlevered it... since that day, I've never overleveraged our business. I don't take on too much debt. I grow with more equity.
advice_items.summary_en: Avoid overleveraging with excessive debt; after Hurricane Katrina nearly broke the business, grow primarily with equity.
advice_items.summary_zh: 切忌过度加杠杆负债扩张，优先用自有股权稳健成长

advice_items.quote: Do one thing and do it better than anybody else. Focus on that. Know what you're good at and execute on a daily basis. Then scale.
advice_items.summary_en: Focus on one core offering and execute it better than anyone else every day instead of branching out prematurely.
advice_items.summary_zh: 聚焦单一核心业务做到极致，每日精进再规模化

advice_items.canonical_tag: Solve Real Pain Points & Deliver Value
advice_items.quote: You have to have an amazing product and service... something that's cravable. If you have a mediocre product, you'll never make it.
advice_items.summary_en: Build an exceptional, cravable core product and service; a mediocre product will never succeed long-term.
advice_items.summary_zh: 必须打造让人上瘾的卓越核心产品，平庸产品必败

advice_items.canonical_tag: Own Equity Rather Than Trading Time
advice_items.quote: Since I own the business, I get to make the right decisions based on the long-term success of the business... I don't have to make short-term decisions to do short-term gains.
advice_items.summary_en: Retain controlling equity ownership (91-92%) so you can prioritize long-term crew and customer health over short-term investor pressure.
advice_items.summary_zh: 紧握控股权，才能做长期正确决策而非迎合短期利益

advice_items.quote: What I can do with hiring people and having a great place to work and what I can do for the money I can give back to communities. That for me just drives me.
advice_items.summary_en: Stay driven by faith and purpose—creating great jobs, serving people, giving back to communities, and leaving the world better.
advice_items.summary_zh: 怀抱回馈社会与服务的使命感，才能永不懈怠

advice_items.canonical_tag: OTHER:Lead by Example & Care for Your Team
advice_items.quote: Lead by example and lead people by their hearts and minds. They see me working in the restaurants... taking care of my crew, so they work hard for me.
advice_items.summary_en: Lead by example from the front lines and take genuine care of your team's hearts and minds so they deliver great service.
advice_items.summary_zh: 以身作则并用心关怀员工，员工才会全力回报

advice_items.quote: I think you learn more from your mistakes than you do from your successes, and we're constantly getting knocked back.
advice_items.summary_en: Expect constant setbacks and learn from mistakes, which teach far more than successes.
advice_items.summary_zh: 从错误和挫折中学到的永远比从成功中学到的更多

advice_items.canonical_tag: Be Careful Who You Partner With
advice_items.quote: There's some bad people out there that want to take advantage of you. Surround yourself by good people. Trust, but verify. And if they screw you over, then move on.
advice_items.summary_en: Surround yourself with good people, trust but verify, and cut ties immediately with anyone who takes advantage of you.
advice_items.summary_zh: 警惕想占便宜的人，信任但要核实，被坑即刻止损

advice_items.quote: Concentrate more on progress rather than perfection... That one training program can be version one. You can be on version 100 a year from now.
advice_items.summary_en: Prioritize progress over perfection; launch version one and iterate instead of stalling your business.
advice_items.summary_zh: 重进步而非求完美，先推第一版再持续迭代优化

advice_items.quote: My best advice I can give a young entrepreneur when they're getting started is never ever ever ever give up... Nothing ever happens unless somebody pursues a vision fanatically.
advice_items.summary_en: Accept extreme hours, pressure, and high risk tolerance early on, pursue your vision fanatically, and never give up.
advice_items.summary_zh: 创业要承受极高压力与牺牲，狂热执着且绝不放弃

advice_items.quote: The only difference between millionaire business owners and billionaire business owners are scale. It's just that want to grow... Grow it and scale it and you'll become a billionaire.
advice_items.summary_en: Once you build a proven million-dollar business, relentless growth and scale are what separate billionaires from millionaires.
advice_items.summary_zh: 百万富翁与亿万富翁的唯一差距在于持续做大规模

advice_items.quote: Always better quality, better service. Even if it cost you more, pays off in the end. So one of our values is sales driven, but still being profit smart.
advice_items.summary_en: In tight-margin businesses (5-10 cents on the dollar), drive high sales volume while staying profit-smart and never cutting quality or service.
advice_items.summary_zh: 薄利靠规模销量取胜，宁可多花成本也要保品质服务

guests.first_money_or_break: 高中大学在餐厅打工积累行业经验，因商业计划被教授打全班最低分且遭当地银行悉数拒贷，只身赴阿拉斯加住帐篷做商业捕鱼攒下约5万美元启动资金，再申请5万美元SBA小企业贷款，亲手翻修破旧店面于1996年创立Raising Cane's。
guests.wealth_detail: North of $20B net worth; $400M highest single-year income; owns 91-92% of Raising Cane's (900+ locations)
guests.zero_start_advice: 若一无所有重启，会继续选择自己熟悉的餐饮业，寻找另一款让人上瘾的爆款单品，聚焦单点做到极致并围绕它组建团队后规模化扩张；没钱且借不到钱时要靠体力劳动自攒本金，并善用SBA贷款、SBDC和SCORE等政府及导师资源。
